# package l2

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-profinet/l2"
```

Package l2 defines the Layer 2 port abstraction PROFINET runs on and a demultiplexer that shares one port between the protocol engines (DCP, LLDP, cyclic RT, alarms, the IP stack of a virtual network).

A [Port](#type-port) sends and receives complete Ethernet frames without FCS. The implementations are:

  - the virtual Ethernet network of package vnet, which needs no privileges and is what the unit and end-to-end tests use;
  - raw packet sockets: AF\_PACKET on Linux (package l2/afpacket), BPF devices on macOS and the BSDs (package l2/bpf) and Npcap on Windows (package l2/npcap), which need the privileges documented in each.

Protocol code depends only on [Port](#type-port), never on an operating system API.

## Functions

### func JoinMulticast

```go
func JoinMulticast(p Port, group ethernet.MAC) error
```

JoinMulticast joins group when p filters multicast frames, and does nothing otherwise.

### type Matcher

```go
type Matcher func(f *ethernet.Frame) bool
```

Matcher selects the frames a [Subscription](#type-subscription) receives. It is called on the demultiplexer's goroutine with a frame that is valid only during the call; it must not block or retain f.

#### func MatchEtherType

```go
func MatchEtherType(t ethernet.EtherType) Matcher
```

MatchEtherType matches frames of one EtherType.

#### func MatchFrameIDs

```go
func MatchFrameIDs(lo, hi uint16) Matcher
```

MatchFrameIDs matches PROFINET frames (EtherType 0x8892) whose FrameID is in \[lo, hi].

### type Mux

```go
type Mux struct {

	// handled counts the frames fully processed (counted, dispatched or
	// dropped): received is counted before that, so tests wait on this.

}
```

Mux shares one [Port](#type-port) between several protocol engines. One goroutine reads frames and copies each into the bounded queue of every subscription that matches it; a full queue drops the frame (and counts it) instead of blocking the port. Sending goes straight to the port.

A Mux is safe for concurrent use.

#### func NewMux

```go
func NewMux(p Port) *Mux
```

NewMux starts demultiplexing frames read from p. It does not take ownership of p: closing the Mux stops the reader; closing p is the caller's job (and also stops the reader).

#### func (Mux) Close

```go
func (m *Mux) Close() error
```

Close stops the reader and closes every subscription. It does not close the port.

#### func (Mux) Done

```go
func (m *Mux) Done() <-chan struct{}
```

Done is closed when the reader stops: after Close, or when the port failed or was closed.

#### func (Mux) Err

```go
func (m *Mux) Err() error
```

Err returns the error that stopped the reader, nil while it runs and after Close.

#### func (Mux) HardwareAddr

```go
func (m *Mux) HardwareAddr() ethernet.MAC
```

HardwareAddr returns the MAC address of the port.

#### func (Mux) Port

Port returns the port the Mux reads from.

#### func (Mux) Subscribe

```go
func (m *Mux) Subscribe(match Matcher, queueLen int) (*Subscription, error)
```

Subscribe registers a subscription for the frames match selects, with a queue of queueLen frames (at least 1). Frames that arrive while the queue is full are dropped.

### type MuxStats

```go
type MuxStats struct {
	// Received is the number of frames read from the port.
	Received uint64
	// Malformed is the number of frames that were too short to decode.
	Malformed uint64
	// Unclaimed is the number of frames no subscription matched.
	Unclaimed uint64
	// Overflow is the number of frames dropped because the queue of a

	Overflow uint64
	// Sent is the number of frames written to the port.
	Sent uint64
}
```

MuxStats are the counters of a [Mux](#type-mux).

### type Port

```go
type Port interface {
	// ReadFrame reads the next frame into p and returns its length. A
	// frame longer than p is truncated to len(p). It returns ctx.Err()
	// when ctx is done first.
	ReadFrame(ctx context.Context, p []byte) (int, error)

	// WriteFrame sends one frame. Frames shorter than
	// ethernet.MinFrameLen are padded by the port. The port does not
	// retain p after WriteFrame returns.
	WriteFrame(ctx context.Context, p []byte) error

	// HardwareAddr returns the port's MAC address, the source address of
	// the frames the protocol engines send.
	HardwareAddr() ethernet.MAC

	// MTU returns the largest payload the port can send in one frame.
	MTU() int

	// Close releases the port.
	Close() error
}
```

Port is an Ethernet port that sends and receives whole frames.

ReadFrame and WriteFrame may be called concurrently with each other; a Port must allow one reader and any number of writers at the same time. Close unblocks a pending ReadFrame, which then returns an error matching profinet.ErrClosed.

### type Subscription

```go
type Subscription struct {
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

Subscription is a bounded queue of frames from a [Mux](#type-mux). Recv must be called from one goroutine at a time.

#### func (Subscription) Close

```go
func (s *Subscription) Close()
```

Close removes the subscription from the Mux.

#### func (Subscription) Done

```go
func (s *Subscription) Done() <-chan struct{}
```

Done is closed when the subscription is closed, by Close or because the Mux stopped.

#### func (Subscription) Overflow

```go
func (s *Subscription) Overflow() uint64
```

Overflow returns the number of frames dropped because the queue was full.

#### func (Subscription) Recv

```go
func (s *Subscription) Recv(ctx context.Context) (ethernet.Frame, error)
```

Recv returns the next frame. The frame and its payload are valid until the next call of Recv or Close. Recv returns ctx.Err() when ctx is done and an error matching profinet.ErrClosed after Close.
